solar_storm.speaker: kenji
solar_storm.quote: Safe mode is the conservative call when solar output drops 30% — if your battery reserve is tight, keeping instruments on can trigger a power blackout.

solar_storm.speaker: ferreira
solar_storm.quote: Storm aurorae and energetic particle fluxes are priceless science — if your power margin exceeds 30% and you fitted a radiation vault, we can ride it out!

solar_storm.speaker: okafor
solar_storm.quote: On a crewed ship, put the astronauts behind the storm shelter walls immediately while keeping minimal telemetry online.

micrometeoroid.speaker: kenji
micrometeoroid.quote: Spend the $5M engineering workaround to bypass the damaged solar string and recover half the lost wattage.

micrometeoroid.speaker: okafor
micrometeoroid.quote: We can feather and re-point the array away from the dust stream — it trims pointing accuracy slightly, but costs $0M and preserves 92% panel health.

micrometeoroid.speaker: hale
micrometeoroid.quote: If you built a generous 25% power margin into your arrays, save the contingency budget and accept the 20% hit.

wheel_failure.speaker: okafor
wheel_failure.quote: Without a redundant wheel, fire the RCS attitude thrusters ($8M ops support) so your telescope and imagers don't blur.

wheel_failure.speaker: ferreira
wheel_failure.quote: Spinning up the redundant reaction wheel keeps our arcsecond pointing locked with zero science loss.

wheel_failure.speaker: hale
wheel_failure.quote: If we're near our budget ceiling and already ahead of our science target, accept the coarser pointing rather than overspending.

ground_outage.speaker: echo
ground_outage.quote: Keep the instruments recording into onboard solid-state memory — as long as your flight computer has ≥ 64 Gb storage, we won't drop a single frame.

ground_outage.speaker: kenji
ground_outage.quote: If your onboard memory buffer is small or nearly full, pause the instruments for 5 days so old high-value data isn't overwritten.

conjunction.speaker: echo
conjunction.quote: With an autonomous AI flight computer on board, upload the 14-day sequence and let the spacecraft observe behind the Sun on its own.

conjunction.speaker: okafor
conjunction.quote: If your flight computer lacks autonomy, do NOT pre-program blind — hold attitude in safe loiter until solar radio noise clears.

radiation_upset.speaker: echo
radiation_upset.quote: Reboot the flight computer immediately! Losing 2 days of observations is much safer than letting a single-event upset corrupt 10% of our science archive.

radiation_upset.speaker: ferreira
radiation_upset.quote: If you installed a radiation-hardened computer (≥ 1,000 krad), its ECC memory scrubs the bit-flip automatically without losing observation time.

crew_illness.speaker: ferreira
crew_illness.quote: Increase daily resistance exercise and reduce workload right away — a 5% science dip is minor compared to astronaut bone loss.

crew_illness.speaker: okafor
crew_illness.quote: Deploy the medical countermeasure kit and tune spin-habitat RPM ($2M ops support) to restore crew health without cutting science.

bonus_discovery.speaker: ferreira
bonus_discovery.quote: Extend operations by 20%! Follow-up spectra on an unexpected discovery are how good missions become legendary.

bonus_discovery.speaker: hale
bonus_discovery.quote: Check your remaining budget and component design life first — if budget is tight, wrap up on schedule and bank the win.

launch_weather.speaker: okafor
launch_weather.quote: Scrub for 24 hours ($3M pad turnaround). Upper-level wind shear can damage solar array hinges if your bus is rated below 6 g.

launch_weather.speaker: hale
launch_weather.quote: If your spacecraft structure is rated for ≥ 6 g, it will shrug off the wind shear without spending $3M.

neg_budget_cut.speaker: ferreira
neg_budget_cut.quote: Science Specialist priority: protect instrument calibration and observation time even if operations reserve shrinks.

neg_budget_cut.speaker: kenji
neg_budget_cut.quote: Flight Engineer priority: protect power and thermal margins so an unexpected storm doesn't end the mission.

neg_budget_cut.speaker: echo
neg_budget_cut.quote: Comms & Resources priority: compress ground-station passes to save $6M immediately.

neg_budget_cut.speaker: hale
neg_budget_cut.quote: Commander compromise: share a 3% trim across all desks so every subsystem stays within operating limits.

neg_bonus_target.speaker: ferreira
neg_bonus_target.quote: Science Specialist priority: slew the spacecraft immediately for +12% bonus science while the plume is active!

neg_bonus_target.speaker: okafor
neg_bonus_target.quote: Flight Engineer priority: hold our nominal attitude and preserve propellant and battery margins.

neg_bonus_target.speaker: echo
neg_bonus_target.quote: Comms & Resources priority: book an emergency high-rate DSN pass ($2M) so our existing buffer is safe first.

neg_bonus_target.speaker: hale
neg_bonus_target.quote: Commander compromise: capture a short 2-hour target-of-opportunity scan (+6% science) without draining the battery.

neg_bandwidth_clash.speaker: ferreira
neg_bandwidth_clash.quote: Science Specialist priority: dedicate 80% of downlink bandwidth to uncompressed science frames (+8% science).

neg_bandwidth_clash.speaker: kenji
neg_bandwidth_clash.quote: Flight Engineer priority: keep continuous engineering telemetry active to guard pointing and thermal stability (+5% pointing).

neg_bandwidth_clash.speaker: echo
neg_bandwidth_clash.quote: Comms & Resources priority: run onboard lossless packet compression for balanced science and telemetry at $0M extra cost.
